subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Aluminum: The Metal That Took a Century to Tame
description: A 60-second lesson on Aluminum: The Metal That Took a Century to Tame.

hook.text: In 1884, the Washington Monument was capped with aluminum. It was more valuable than gold.

buildup.text: Aluminum is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust. But it bonds so tightly to oxygen that extraction was nearly impossible.

discovery.text: The Hall-Héroult process, invented in 1886, uses electricity to separate aluminum from bauxite ore.

twist.text: Napoleon III served honored guests on aluminum plates. Less important guests got gold ones.

climax.text: Today, aluminum costs $2 per kilogram. It's in every airplane, soda can, and smartphone.

punchline.text: Once rarer than gold. Now it wraps your leftovers.

quiz.question: Why was aluminum once more valuable than gold?
options: It was only found in a single mine in Greenland
It bonds tightly to oxygen, making extraction nearly impossible
Royal families hoarded all known aluminum supplies
